decision_log.decision: Table runs along the room's long axis (x), centred at x 2.40, 2.40 x 0.84 m.
decision_log.rationale: This is the only orientation that seats eight in a 3.60 m wide room while keeping a continuous route along one long wall between the two short-wall doors.

decision_log.decision: Built-in banquette on the north wall seating four, 0.49 m deep.
decision_log.rationale: Meets the built-in seating requirement and saves roughly 0.40 m of depth compared with a second row of chairs, which is what makes a 1.80 m clear corridor possible.

decision_log.decision: Two built-in sideboards flank the banquette at 0.90 m counter height, filling the north wall end to end.
decision_log.rationale: One continuous joinery wall gives a serving counter beside the kitchen door, glassware and linen storage, and closes the bench ends; it is the principal elevation.

decision_log.decision: Kitchen door on the west short wall and hall door on the east short wall, both centred at y 0.90 at the south end of their walls.
decision_log.rationale: Both doors land at the ends of the corridor so the route is straight and both inward swing arcs fall within the corridor, well clear of every piece of furniture.

decision_log.decision: Circulation corridor 1.80 m wide along the south wall (centreline y 0.90; nearest furniture at y 1.81).
decision_log.rationale: Gives 0.90 m of clear floor on each side of the centreline, so the brief's 0.90 m minimum is met under either reading of the clearance rule.

decision_log.decision: Four chairs on the south side only, no end chairs.
decision_log.rationale: Leaves both table ends open: the west end is the service landing from the kitchen and the entry to the banquette, the east end gives access to the east sideboard; end chairs would also have trapped the corner banquette seats.

decision_log.decision: Window band on the south wall, 2.40 m wide, matched to the table length, sill 0.95 m, head 2.10 m.
decision_log.rationale: Provides the second opening and daylight directly opposite the banquette; the head aligns with the door heads to keep a single datum under the low ceiling.

decision_log.decision: Light envelope (pale oak floor, chalk walls, soft-white ceiling) with the darker moss-grey joinery held below 1.05 m.
decision_log.rationale: A 2.40 m ceiling reads taller when the upper two thirds of the room are light; the dark joinery forms a low datum band that anchors the bench wall.

decision_log.decision: Single linear pendant with underside at 1.55 m, plus concealed shelf strip, two wall lights and two corridor downlights.
decision_log.rationale: One low linear fitting lights the whole 2.40 m table evenly without a cluster of pendants under a low ceiling; the other circuits give task and ambient layers.

decision_log.decision: No mirrored panels anywhere; walls in matt clay paint, joinery in matt eggshell.
decision_log.rationale: Complies with the brief's must-not list: no mirrored wall panels and no high-gloss lacquer on any wall surface.

decision_log.decision: Floor finish is engineered oak plank, 180 mm boards, matt hardwax oil, laid along x.
decision_log.rationale: Names material and finish as required; long boards along the room length stretch the plan visually and the matt oil suits a room where chairs move daily.
